title: What is a dominator tree, and why does every optimizer query it?

cast.name: Ravi
cast.role: LLVM maintainer who asks one question at a time

glossary.full: First blocks a block no longer dominates
A merge that picks a value by the incoming edge
glossary.note: Sits at the start of a join block.

key_points: X dominates Y when every path from the entry to Y goes through X.
The immediate dominators form a tree that many passes query.
The dominance frontier is where phi nodes are placed.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Four blocks. Ravi hands Priya a pencil and one question.

beats.speaker: ravi
beats.text: Rule: block X dominates block Y if every path from the entry A to Y goes through X.

visuals.text: X dominates Y: every path from A to Y passes through X

beats.speaker: ravi
beats.text: Question: which block is the closest dominator of D? B, C or A?

beats.speaker: ravi
beats.text: Guess before I flip the card.

visuals.sub: skipped by the path A, C, D
skipped by the path A, B, D

beats.speaker: ravi
beats.text: One path goes A, C, D and never touches B. Another goes A, B, D and never touches C. Only A is on every path.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.text: So A is D's parent in the dominator tree?

beats.speaker: ravi
beats.text: Yes. Link each block to its immediate dominator and you get a tree rooted at the entry.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.text: What is a tree like that good for?

beats.speaker: ravi
beats.text: Passes ask it constantly. Is a definition above every use? Can this code hoist out of a loop? Is that edge a loop back to a dominator?

visuals.text: SSA validity · loop hoisting · value numbering · loop detection

beats.speaker: ravi
beats.text: And D is where B and C stop dominating. That frontier is exactly where a phi node belongs.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.text: Cooper, Harvey and Kennedy build this tree fast?

beats.speaker: ravi
beats.text: By visiting blocks in reverse postorder and intersecting each block's predecessors' answers, until nothing changes.
